messages.author: 98f40a40fc5442e5
messages.subject: Sampling
parts:
Hi,

I'm a datascientist. I mostly use R and Weka in my daily work. I've tried Rattle to see if it could help me improve my performance by getting a quicker insight when I address new data.

Unfortunately, I'm stuck on the problem of sampling, particularly when facing an imbalanced dataset: for instance, I used the "weather" dataset which has 215 negative instances for only 41 positive instances. So applying any of the proposed machine learning algorithms on this dataset results in erroneous/biaised results.

As a consequence, I I wanted to use the classical method that consists in over/under-sampling the instances.

But if I've found the very basic options in the "data" tab to:
(1) split the dataset into train/test/validation sets and
(2) add a formula to add some weights to the instances.
unfortunately, I haven't found any possibility to apply over/under sampling.

Is there any way to do so (or is it what the formula for adding weights does?)?

By the way, sampling is a very important phase when preparing data, so I would have created a specialized tab for this process.


Finally thanks for your work on this great tool for teaching/demonstrating ML!

messages.author: 22df2884417c9d57
messages.subject: Re: Sampling
parts:
Hi,

The weather dataset has the rain today and tomorrow set at greater than 1mm, you can recode it to be 0, then you get a lot more positives.

You can also use the weatherAUS file, that has lots more locations, it is under library

Regards
Tony
